result:
All 113 tests in `StringUtilsAgentTest` pass against the documented contract of `StringUtils`.

Summary: I wrote a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (`src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/StringUtilsAgentTest.java`) covering ~110 cases across most of `StringUtils`' public methods (abbreviate, capitalize, center, chomp/chop, compare, contains*, countMatches, default*, difference, equals*, firstNon*, getCommonPrefix, getLevenshteinDistance, indexOf*/ordinalIndexOf, is* predicates, join, left/right/mid, leftPad/rightPad, normalizeSpace, overlay, remove*, repeat, replace*, reverse/rotate, split*, startsWith/endsWith*, strip*, substring*, swapCase, toCodePoints, trim*, truncate, unwrap/wrap*, upper/lowerCase, length, valueOf), with emphasis on null/empty/negative/boundary inputs and documented exception cases.

No bugs were found — every assertion, once corrected to match the method's documented contract, passes against the actual implementation. The four initial failures were all mistakes in my own test data (wrong expected values I had miscalculated), not defects in `StringUtils`; after fixing those expected values, the full suite is green.
